subject: SS
title: Reading the social pyramid
teach: A social class is a group with a similar position in society. A social pyramid shows rank: a small group at the top had more power; larger groups lower down had less power.
Read the Ancient Egyptian Society handout’s five diagram labels from top to bottom: Pharaoh; Priests and nobles; Traders, artisans, shopkeepers, and scribes; Farmers and herders; Unskilled workers.

The diagram’s bottom label is Unskilled workers. The readings also discuss enslaved people and servants below farmers. Do not replace the diagram’s exact label when the question asks for that diagram. Lower rank does not mean work was unimportant.

The assigned WCS OER pyramid on page 15 groups soldiers and scribes together. The separate Ancient Egyptian Society handout groups scribes with traders, artisans and shopkeepers. Use the named diagram when answering a question.

example.prompt: In the Ancient Egyptian Society handout pyramid, were scribes above or below farmers?
example.thinking: Find each labeled level. Scribes share a level with traders, artisans and shopkeepers. Farmers and herders are one level below.
example.answer: Scribes were above farmers in the Ancient Egyptian Society handout pyramid.
example.why: The answer uses the labeled levels. It does not claim that farming was unimportant.

teachingSections.tryPrompt: Who is at the top of the Ancient Egyptian Society handout pyramid?
teachingSections.tryAnswer: Pharaoh. The Ancient Egyptian Society handout pyramid places the ruler above the other social groups.

connections.prompt: Why did people high on the social pyramid still depend on farmers?
options: Farmers supplied food needed across social classes.
High rank meant people did not need any food.
Farmers had the most political power in every period.
connections.rationale: Farmers supplied food needed across social classes. Read the Ancient Egyptian Society handout pyramid, then connect each labeled group with its work.

connections.prompt: A school chart places a principal above several roles. What is a limit of comparing it with Egypt’s pyramid?
options: Both show roles, but a school chart is not ancient Egypt’s social-class system.
Both show that lower positions contribute nothing useful.
Both mean every person below the top performs one identical job.
connections.rationale: Both show roles, but a school chart is not ancient Egypt’s social-class system. A comparison can show one relationship without making two societies identical.

vocabulary.definition: Groups in a society with similar social position.
